message.content:
Closures get changed all the time—sometimes multiple times in a single day. The authorities might expand a no-fly zone because of a protest or a fire, or they might shorten a closure’s end time if the weather clears up unexpectedly. Sometimes they even add new ones suddenly, like when a military exercise starts without warning.

Dispatchers have to keep an eye on these updates because a drone already in the air might suddenly be flying through a restricted area. If that happens, we have to call the flight back or reroute it—if we can—before it gets into trouble. It’s a constant headache.
